subject.title: Org claim: vmware-aiops + vmware-monitor — @kingaiwork lookalikes impersonate @zw008 listings (same pattern as #2966/#3035)

question: Do the verified production records and audit history support hiding or renaming both @kingaiwork VMware listings, and does the repeated pattern warrant broader publisher enforcement?
rationale: The source tree defines the available moderation mechanisms, but only authorized staff can validate current production state, preserve non-public evidence, and choose proportional listing- or account-level enforcement.

options.title: Quarantine and review publisher
options.body: Preserve evidence, hide both disputed listings, verify installation recovery, and conduct an account-wide review before deciding broader sanctions.

options.title: Rename the disputed listings
options.body: Require non-conflicting slugs and accurate metadata while retaining the resources if staff finds their underlying content permissible.

options.title: Leave listings unchanged
options.body: Keep the resources public only if production evidence does not substantiate impersonation or misleading marketplace behavior.

recommendation.title: Quarantine and review publisher
recommendation.body: Preserve evidence, hide both disputed listings, verify installation recovery, and conduct an account-wide review before deciding broader sanctions.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest repository-history signal is the merged org and namespace claim-intake and policy-routing work.
